item.title: Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05%
item.description: By Ozumba Chika Tony Elumelu, Chairman of Heirs Holdings, has increased his stake in Seplat Energy Plc to 22.05 per cent following the acquisition of additional shares valued at approximately $70 million. The latest purchase, made through Heirs Energies Limited, involved 5,888,341 ordinary shares, representing about one per cent of the company. The transaction was disclosed to the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday in a notification signed by Edith Onwuchekwa, Seplat Energy’s Director, Legal and Company Secretary. According to the disclosure, Heirs Energies Limited, a company controlled by Elumelu, acquired the shares from the company. Following the transaction, Heirs Energies’ direct shareholding in Seplat rose to 33,832,208 shares. The disclosure added that entities controlled by Elumelu — Heirs Energies Limited and Heirs Holdings Limited — now hold a combined 132,288,341 shares, representing a voting interest of 22.05 per cent of Seplat’s issued share capital of 599,944,561 shares. The company said the notification was made in compliance with Rule 17.15(c) of the NGX Rulebook 2015 on disclosure of dealings in issuers’ shares and Article 19(3) of the United Kingdom Market Abuse Regulations. The latest acquisition follows a similar transaction in September, when Elumelu, through Heirs Energies, purchased six million Seplat shares for £53.2 million. That transaction raised the combined shareholding of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings in the company to 21.07 per cent. Meanwhile, Seplat also disclosed a separate insider transaction involving its Chairman, Udoma Udo Udoma. The company said Tierce Investments Limited, a firm wholly owned by Udoma, purchased Seplat Energy’s 9.125 per cent Senior Unsecured Notes due March 21, 2030. The notes had a face value of $370,000, while the cash consideration for the purchase was $397,076.81. The post Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22.05% appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Passenger vows never to fly United Nigeria Airlines over early departure – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has said a passenger sent him a message last week threatening never to fly with the airline again because it departed earlier than its advertised time. Okonkwo said the passenger complained that while United Nigeria Airlines advertised an 11:30am departure, it took off at 11:20am. He spoke during a dialogue on Responsible Business Communication: Building Trust and Financing Investments for Sustainable Human Development at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, in Abuja, where he urged organisations to always tell the truth, saying it was the best reputation management strategy. He said: “A typical Nigerian traveller has his mind set on the timely departure of the airline, and if anything happens, you have to communicate the truth. You may have an AOG, technical issues, and sometimes that message doesn’t really sink. “I had a passenger last week who sent me a message saying they will never fly United Nigeria Airlines anymore and I said, why? He said, because they left on time. He said United Nigeria Airlines advertised departure for 11:30am but departed at 11:20am, and as the chairman, I was actually worried about how to respond. “I wanted to get angry, I wanted to shout back at him. But again, my experience being a member of this forum came into play, and I simply sent him a message saying, ‘I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.’ That was my answer. He never got back.” He also recounted an incident in which UNA diverted to Asaba instead of Abuja, saying the aircraft was scheduled to fly from Lagos to Abuja but landed in Asaba following an error by the dispatcher, who mistakenly entered Asaba as the destination in the flight documentation. He said the pilots followed the destination indicated in the documents and landed accordingly, while the cabin crew, believing they had arrived in Abuja, welcomed passengers to the Federal Capital Territory. According to him, the incident itself was not necessarily a major crisis until the airline’s communication team issued an inaccurate explanation. Okonkwo said the airline’s communication team, in an attempt to protect the company’s reputation, attributed the incident to bad weather in Abuja, despite the fact that the aircraft had landed in Asaba because of an error in its flight documentation. He, however, maintained that organisations must not confuse reputation protection with withholding or manipulating facts, warning that attempts to conceal the truth could eventually cause greater damage than the original crisis. He added that telling verified truths demonstrates respect for stakeholders and helps build confidence in an organisation, irrespective of how uncomfortable the information might be. He said: “The best word of public relations is to tell the truth and challenge responsibly. item.title: 2027: Kalu promises Tinubu 75% votes in South-East
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Chief Benjamin Kalu, has assured President Bola Tinubu that the South-East will deliver 75 per cent of its votes to him in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the President should not have to negotiate for 25 per cent support in the zone. Kalu gave the assurance during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Abia State, where he said party members were mobilising voters across communities to secure Tinubu’s re-election. He said the APC was going from house to house and village to village to canvass support for the President, adding that the party was determined to demonstrate its electoral strength in the state. According to him, Tinubu has attracted several infrastructural interventions and political appointments to the South-East and would do more if re-elected. Kalu said: “Mr President, the numbers you have in Abia will give you the votes you are looking for. Nobody should convert you to a beggar of 25 per cent. “We have about 12.3 million voters in Abia State. We have millions of members of APC. We have told ourselves that each person will bring 10 people, 10 voters to vote for you. And that will give us 1,620,000 and more votes for you. “That is about 75 per cent of the votes registered voters in Abia State. Mr President, let nobody deceive you that he is working to get 25 per cent for you in Abia.” The Deputy Speaker also disclosed that supporters had assembled 100 branded vehicles for distribution across the state as part of the campaign mobilisation. He said the January 16 election would provide an opportunity for the people of Abia to demonstrate their appreciation for Tinubu’s interventions. Kalu dismissed suggestions that the APC lacked a significant presence in Abia, pointing to the turnout at the rally as evidence of the party’s support base. “We are not sleeping. We are going from house to house. We are going from village to village. We are going from community to community. We are not playing our politics in Abuja,” he said. The APC governorship candidate in Abia State, Chief Eric Opah, also expressed confidence in the party’s growing support base, assuring that its members were committed to Tinubu’s re-election. Similarly, party stakeholders from the three senatorial districts — Chief Emeka Stanley of Abia South, Hon. Cosmas Ndukwe of Abia North and Chief Henry Ikoh of Abia Central — pledged their support for the President, citing his administration’s interventions in the South-East. The Managing Director of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), Chief Mark Okoye, said Tinubu had demonstrated commitment to the development of the region through the establishment of the commission. Earlier, the Abia APC Chairman and state coordinator of the presidential campaign, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, declared that the state was an APC stronghold and pledged that it would deliver 90 per cent of its votes to Tinubu.

item.title: Reps to probe 22 states over unpaid pensions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate reports that 22 states are failing to pay retirement benefits regularly, amid concerns over the hardship facing thousands of pensioners across the country. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Rep. Adesola Adebayo, representing Apapa Federal Constituency of Lagos State, at plenary on Tuesday. Moving the motion, Adebayo cited a report indicating that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states pay pensions regularly, while the remaining 22 owe retirees several months or, in some cases, years of outstanding entitlements. He described pensions as an earned right rather than a privilege or charity, arguing that public servants who had devoted between 30 and 35 years to service deserved to receive their retirement benefits without unnecessary hardship. The lawmaker expressed concern that many pensioners aged between 70 and 90 were struggling to afford food, medication, rent and other basic necessities, with some reportedly dying in poverty. He also criticised prolonged verification exercises that require elderly retirees to queue for hours or days under harsh weather conditions, citing reports of pensioners collapsing and dying during such exercises. Adebayo argued that the failure to pay pensions undermined constitutional provisions and human dignity, while creating anxiety among serving public workers about their prospects after retirement. The motion, however, generated debate among lawmakers over the constitutional powers of the National Assembly to intervene in pension matters involving state governments. Opposing the motion, Rep. Mark Essiet argued that pension obligations of state governments fell within the jurisdiction of state authorities and their respective Houses of Assembly. He cautioned against any proposal for the Federal Government to deduct funds from states’ allocations to settle outstanding pension liabilities, describing such a move as unconstitutional. Rep. Umoh urged the House to focus on the pension challenges facing military personnel, who, he said, had repeatedly protested over their entitlements. Similarly, Rep. Dominic Okafor cautioned against generalising the allegations against all states, noting that some governors had fulfilled their pension obligations. He cited Anambra State as an example, arguing that the motion should distinguish between states with outstanding pension liabilities and those meeting their responsibilities. However, Rep. Billy Owasaro urged lawmakers not to abandon the motion but to amend provisions that might fall outside the constitutional powers of the National Assembly. He said the plight of elderly pensioners was too serious to be ignored. “We know what our fathers are going through. item.title: Reps move to protect Nigerians displaced by Gabon demolition
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for urgent intervention to protect thousands of Nigerians, particularly Ilaje fishermen, reportedly displaced after authorities in Gabon demolished their homes and business premises. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Donald Ojogo at plenary on Tuesday. Presenting the motion, Ojogo expressed concern over the fate of thousands of Nigerians who were reportedly displaced last week following the demolition of their residences along Gabon’s fishing coast. He said the affected Nigerians, predominantly of Ilaje extraction, had lived and conducted fishing and related businesses in Gabon for decades. The lawmaker warned that the demolition had left many of them homeless and exposed to health risks and other humanitarian challenges. He said the situation required urgent diplomatic intervention by the Nigerian Government to prevent further hardship and ensure that the rights and welfare of the affected citizens were protected. Ojogo maintained that the government had a responsibility to safeguard Nigerians wherever they resided, including those living and working outside the country. He cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, as well as the provisions of Chapter II on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy. The lawmaker also drew attention to regional protocols governing the Gulf of Guinea, particularly provisions relating to the protection of marine resources and fishing activities. The House unanimously adopted the motion through a voice vote, urging the Federal Government to establish the circumstances surrounding the demolition and take necessary steps to protect the welfare and rights of the affected Nigerians. It subsequently mandated its Committees on Foreign Affairs, Diaspora, Inland Waterways, and Cooperation and Integration in Africa to urgently intervene and investigate the circumstances surrounding the displacement. The committees are also expected to ascertain the welfare and living conditions of the affected Nigerians, particularly the Ilaje fishermen, and submit their findings to the House within 14 legislative days. item.title: 2027: Anambra set for Tinubu campaign rally
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State is preparing to host a mega campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, with members of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) expected to participate. The rally, tagged “SoluTinubu 2027”, is scheduled to hold on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka. According to the state’s Presidential Campaign Council, the event is expected to attract party members from the 326 political wards across Anambra State and demonstrate the level of support for Tinubu’s re-election campaign. The organisers said the rally was anchored on the mantra of “progressives working together”, a political message being promoted by Governor Chukwuma Soludo. Preparations for the event are already underway, with Dr Alex Ekwueme Square and its surroundings undergoing decoration ahead of the rally. The event is also expected to attract prominent political figures from across the South-East and other parts of the country, as supporters are expected to use the gathering to publicly declare their backing for Tinubu ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. item.title: Adeboye to commission dialysis centre at UBTH
item.description: By Olayinka Latona BENIN CITY — The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, is expected to commission the Enoch and Folu Adeboye Dialysis Centre at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital (UBTH) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The facility, an intervention by His Love Foundation, the church’s Christian Social Responsibility arm, is aimed at expanding access to kidney care and strengthening dialysis services at the hospital. According to a statement signed by Pastor Bode Olojede, Pastor-in-Charge of RCCG Region 38, Benin City, the commissioning ceremony will be performed by Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, at the hospital premises. The centre is expected to provide dialysis services for patients living with kidney disease and requiring regular treatment, while increasing UBTH’s capacity to attend to patients from Edo State and neighbouring communities. The statement said the project was part of the foundation’s humanitarian interventions, which cover healthcare, education, feeding programmes, social enterprise, environmental architecture, prison impact and rehabilitation. It added that the foundation’s activities extend across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, with interventions in 650 local government areas. According to the statement, the dialysis centre reflects the foundation’s commitment to translating its Christian social responsibility objectives into practical interventions that address healthcare and other social needs. His Love Foundation was established by the RCCG to support individuals, families and communities through interventions in healthcare, education, social welfare, environmental architecture and rehabilitation. item.title: Making better money decisions in 2027 (2)
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor In the first part of this article, I said the first financial goal you should set for 2027 is to have a note to record all your income and expenses, if you are not already doing so. Let me explain how to create the note. The note will contain three columns. The first column is for numbering, the second column will contain the list of expenses, including income, with abbreviations for each of them. The third column will contain what you spent on each item for the day. Some items on the list will have zero expenses for most of the month (for example, capital projects), because these are not things you spend money on regularly. However, items you spend money on regularly, such as food and transportation, will have figures for each day. At the end of each day, or whenever you spend money, open the note and record what you spent on each item. (See the figure for a sample of the note.) Thus, at the end of the day, month or year, this note will help you know how much you earned, how much you spent and what you spent it on. I consider the habit of keeping a daily record of how you spend money the beginning, and perhaps the most important key, to making better money decisions. First, it makes you more conscious of how you spend money and automatically compels you to be careful and more considerate about what you spend money on. This habit also helps you identify unnecessary spending and, hence, reduce it. Most importantly, the record helps you know if you are spending more than your income and compels you to find ways to cut down your expenses and/or increase your income. The second financial goal you need to set to make better money decisions in 2027 is to ensure that you do not spend all your income and that you always save a specific portion of it. This is very empowering, beyond your imagination. The habit of not spending all your income compels you to focus your money on your most important needs. It gives you the discipline to avoid non-essential spending. When you begin to do this, you will soon realise that a significant amount of your money has been going into things you can really do without. In this regard, you can decide to always save 5% of your income. When you master this habit, you can increase it to 10%. item.title: 2027: INEC cautions against unofficial election results
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says independent election results tabulation must complement, not replace, its statutory collation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, stated this on Tuesday in Abuja at a stakeholder roundtable organised by Yiaga Africa to develop a Code of Conduct for Independent Election Results Tabulation. Amupitan, represented by the commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Bayo Boyode, said independent tabulation should promote transparency without creating competing centres of authority. He said the credibility of elections depended not only on voting but also on the accuracy and transparency of vote counting, collation and declaration of results. “The proposed Code of Conduct represents an opportunity to strengthen electoral transparency, promote responsible information management and reinforce public confidence in the integrity of election outcomes. “Independent tabulation must not be presented as a substitute for the statutory collation process, nor should unofficial projections or privately aggregated figures be communicated as officially declared election results. “The Commission’s position is clear: Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” he said. Amupitan said INEC was strengthening the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) and validation checks to improve the traceability of election results. He, however, noted that technology alone could not guarantee credible elections without sound procedures and responsible conduct by political actors. He urged participants to develop practical standards around six guiding principles, including methodological integrity, data security and safeguards against artificial intelligence-driven disinformation. Also speaking, Chairman of Yiaga Africa’s Board, Dr Abdul Hussaini, said the roundtable was organised in response to growing interest in independent citizen-led election results tabulation. He said differences in methodology and the potential misuse of artificial intelligence could undermine electoral integrity and national security if not properly regulated. Hussaini said the proposed code would establish common standards for organisations involved in independent tabulation while recognising INEC as the sole statutory authority responsible for declaring election results. In his keynote address, Chairman of the Editorial Board of ThisDay Newspapers, Mr Oluṣẹgun Adeniyi, called for a voluntary code addressing methodology, sampling, artificial intelligence and election-related violence. In an address titled “Navigating the Promise, Perils and Politics of Independent Result Tabulation in 2027 Election”, Adeniyi said safeguards were necessary to protect ballot integrity and public confidence. item.title: 2027: ‘Prove ADC armed youths against Tinubu’s convoy or withdraw allegation’ – Atiku camp
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The ADC Presidential Campaign Council has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored youths to attack President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Abuja or withdraw the allegation. The Council said the ruling party could not accuse its opponents of arming youths and organising violence without identifying the alleged sponsors and providing evidence, questioning why those arrested over the incident were released if the APC had credible information against them. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the Council was reacting to allegations by the APC Presidential Campaign Council, through its spokesperson, Dele Alake, that the ADC and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) sponsored youths to disrupt campaign rallies and pelt Tinubu’s convoy with stones. Shaibu challenged the APC to explain what happened to those arrested over the alleged attack, raising questions about conflicting accounts from the Presidency and the ruling party. “The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe? “If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents.” The Council denied sponsoring violence or recruiting young Nigerians to confront political opponents, condemning attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, regardless of political affiliation. It also challenged the APC to account for reports and images of money allegedly distributed at its campaign events, arguing that the ruling party could not dismiss every expression of public anger as an opposition-sponsored protest. “Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” Shaibu said. The Council blamed the administration’s policies for worsening the cost of food, fuel and other basic necessities, arguing that campaign inducements would not erase the hardship confronting Nigerians. It urged the APC to substantiate its allegations or withdraw them, insisting that Nigerians would ultimately judge the Tinubu administration by its performance, not accusations against political opponents. item.title: Senate confirms six NMDPRA executive directors
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has confirmed the appointments of six Executive Directors of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The confirmation followed the consideration and adoption of a report by the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas), presented by Senator Suleiman Kawu (Kano South), on Tuesday. Those confirmed for reappointment are Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts; Ogbugo Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure; and Dr Mustapha Lamorde, Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community. The three nominees approved for new appointments are Mobolaji Musa, Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installation and Partnership; Ogechukwu Modie, Executive Director, Economic Regulation and Strategic Planning; and Said Abutalib, Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration. The confirmation followed a request by President Bola Tinubu to the Senate to screen and confirm the appointments of the executive directors and the Secretary of the NMDPRA Board. Tinubu’s request was conveyed in a letter addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio and read during plenary last week. In the letter, the President said the appointments were made pursuant to Section 41, subsections (2) and (3) of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021. He urged the Senate to consider and confirm the nominees expeditiously. Akpabio subsequently referred the request to the Senate Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) for legislative consideration and directed them to report back to plenary within one week. item.title: Enyimba: I’ll help Otti restore club’s glory, Kalu vows
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North, has pledged to assist Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, in reviving Enyimba International Football Club and restoring the club to its former glory. Kalu said he would be willing to serve as a technical adviser or special adviser on the club if Otti considered him suitable for the role. Speaking on Tuesday while answering questions from journalists after receiving the Senate Press Corps’ Best Impactful Representation Award, the former Abia State governor said he was ready to bring his experience in managing the club to bear on efforts to reposition it. He said, “After Governor Otti wins again, he will look into Enyimba. I will be his technical adviser on Enyimba to bring the club back to glory.” Kalu attributed Enyimba’s achievements during his tenure as governor to discipline, effective management and commitment, recalling that he made two major promises to the people of Abia State when he sought election in 1998. According to him, the promises were to build a standard stadium in Aba and transform Enyimba into champions of the African Club Championship, both of which he said he fulfilled. He noted that the club subsequently established itself as a dominant force in Nigerian football, winning the league title for about five or six consecutive seasons and lifting the FA Cup. Recalling his personal involvement in the club’s activities, Kalu said discipline and commitment were central to its success, adding that he regularly travelled from Umuahia to Aba early in the morning to train with the players before resuming official duties. “When I was going to be governor in 1998, there were two promises I made to Aba and the Nigerian people. I told my people in Aba that I would build a proper stadium, which I did. I also told the people of Aba that we were going to become champions of the African Cup of Champions. I asked them to vote for me, promising that they would get it. And I fulfilled that promise,” he said. On his commitment to the club, he added: “Discipline is everything. I used to leave Umuahia at quarter to five every morning and arrive in Aba at 5:30am. I would train with the Enyimba players at 7:30am and return by 8am to take my bath and resume work in the office.” The senator, who expressed concern over what he described as a poor working culture in the country, said Nigeria needed a comprehensive reorientation and fundamental reforms across its institutions. “The working system is very bad, not only in football but in every aspect of our national life. We need reorientation and surgical operations in our system, from beginning to end,” he said. Kalu also commended Rangers International Football Club for its recent performances in continental competitions, expressing hope that the Enugu-based side would sustain its progress. He said he would like to see another Nigerian club win a continental title, noting that several domestic sides had made attempts to achieve the feat.

item.title: Senate approves N100.5bn refund to Yobe for Damaturu airport
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has approved a N100.5 billion Promissory Note Programme to reimburse the Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu. The approval followed the consideration of a report by the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, presented on Tuesday by its Chairman, Senator Aliyu Wamakko (APC, Sokoto North). The committee was mandated to verify the project cost put at N100,509,017,234.55 following a request by President Bola Tinubu, which was referred to it on October 13. Presenting the report, Wamakko said the Yobe State Government embarked on the airport project to address security challenges, improve air connectivity in the North-East and facilitate the evacuation of agricultural produce. He added that the facility was also designed to support humanitarian operations and stimulate economic activities in Yobe and neighbouring states. According to him, the airport features a 3.6-kilometre runway equipped with a Category II Instrument Landing System, taxiways and other essential aviation infrastructure. He said the facility also has an apron capable of accommodating four Boeing 747 aircraft, a terminal building and a cargo shed. Other facilities, he noted, include an air traffic control tower, fire station, perimeter fencing, navigational aids and aeronautical ground lighting. Wamakko disclosed that the Yobe State Government formally requested the Federal Government’s takeover of the airport in a letter dated March 12, 2024, in line with aviation policies governing the ownership and operation of international airports across the country. He said the Federal Executive Council approved the takeover on August 21, subject to verification of the project’s cost and reimbursement to the state government. The senator explained that the reimbursement would be facilitated through a Promissory Note Programme after the relevant government agencies completed their verification and due-process assessments. He said the committee confirmed that the N100.5 billion project cost had undergone a technical audit by the Federal Ministry of Aviation, while the Bureau of Public Procurement conducted a due-process review and issued a Certificate of No Objection on February 25. According to him, the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority also confirmed that the runway, safety facilities and navigational aids complied with international aviation standards. The report further indicated that the airport had been completed and was operational, with test flights conducted by the NCAA ahead of its formal takeover by the Federal Government. With the Senate’s approval, the Federal Government now has the necessary legislative backing to reimburse the Yobe State Government through the Promissory Note Programme. item.title: 2027: Tinubu has no serious rival, Orji Kalu declares
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Senator Orji Uzor Kalu (APC, Abia North) has declared that President Bola Tinubu has no serious challenger ahead of the 2027 presidential election, describing the contest as a race of “Tinubu versus Tinubu”. Kalu, a former governor of Abia State and Chairman of the Senate Committee on South East Development Commission, said the opposition parties had failed to present a credible alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He also dismissed the planned November 23 meeting of opposition presidential candidates to sign a Covenant for Democratic Renewal, describing the proposed coalition meeting as belated. Speaking with journalists on Tuesday, the former Senate Chief Whip challenged opposition politicians seeking to unseat Tinubu to stop what he described as endless political manoeuvring and tell Nigerians what they would do differently if elected. He argued that opposition parties had devoted too much attention to political alliances and criticism of the APC without offering concrete solutions to the country’s challenges. “If I am in opposition and running for president, I will set an alternative agenda for Nigeria to see what I will do. We want to see an alternative agenda,” he said. Kalu challenged opposition candidates to explain how they intended to address insecurity, economic difficulties and other national problems rather than repeatedly accusing the ruling party of being jittery. “Not every day you pay journalists like you to go and say APC is jittery. Where are we jittery? Jittery for whom? How can a lion fear a lamb?” he asked. He maintained that the proposed opposition coalition had come too late to pose a serious challenge to the APC, arguing that the parties should have agreed on a common candidate much earlier. According to him, a sincere agreement among opposition parties at an earlier stage could have raised concerns within the ruling party, even if it did not guarantee their victory. “I thought they could have sincerely come together, presented one presidential candidate. That would have made us start having headaches. Not that they would win,” he said. Dismissing the significance of the November 23 meeting, Kalu said the opposition parties had allowed their internal disagreements to undermine their chances of forming a formidable coalition. “The meeting has no meaning to people like me. If people cannot sit and agree to work together, is it in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, when everybody is fighting to escape, that they will agree on who is going to be the presidential candidate now? The game is too late for them,” he said. He added: “The election is Tinubu versus Tinubu. Tinubu is running against Tinubu. That is the truth. Tinubu beats Tinubu. That is what it is on the ground today, if you understand this politics.” Kalu, who recalled his own presidential ambition in 2007, said his political experience informed his assessment of the emerging opposition coalition. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State. item.title: Tinubu Approves Establishment Of Kebbi Inland Dry Port
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the establishment of an inland dry port in Kebbi State as part of efforts to boost economic activities and improve trade in the state. The President announced the approval on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital. He also pledged to approve additional road infrastructure projects for the state following requests by Governor Nasir Idris. The rally, held at the Birnin Kebbi Stadium, attracted thousands of APC supporters who gathered to express their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Vice President Kashim Shettima and other party leaders were also present at the event, which featured speeches and goodwill messages from party chieftains. ﻿ Speaking at the rally, Governor Idris expressed satisfaction with the turnout and pledged that Kebbi State would deliver 100 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in the 2027 election. Also addressing the crowd, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulazeez Yari, said the President had done much for the North-West, including Kebbi State. Yari attributed the large turnout to Tinubu’s acceptance in the region, citing the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway project, which he said would pass through more than 200 kilometres of Kebbi State. In his remarks, Shettima urged residents of the North to support Tinubu’s re-election, recalling the President’s support for the late President Muhammadu Buhari, who governed Nigeria for eight years. He said Tinubu had stood by Buhari during his political journey and throughout his administration. Taking the podium, Tinubu thanked the people of Kebbi for their support and commended Governor Idris for his leadership. He subsequently announced the approval of some federal projects requested by the governor, including the establishment of the Kebbi Inland Dry Port. The rally also featured goodwill messages from the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the Deputy President of the Senate and other APC leaders and supporters. item.title: Radda Warns Against ‘419 Politicians’ As Supporters Rally For APC In Katsina
item.description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has urged voters to reject what he described as “419 politicians” in the 2027 general elections, declaring that only leaders with proven records of service deserve the people’s mandate. The governor appealed on Tuesday during the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council rally at the Mai’adua International Border Market in Mai’adua Local Government Area, where thousands of APC supporters gathered as the campaign tour continued across the Daura Senatorial Zone. Addressing the enthusiastic crowd, Governor Radda said the massive turnout reflected public confidence in his administration’s performance, particularly in healthcare delivery, education, teacher recruitment, youth empowerment and other development programmes. Supporters rally for Tinubu in Katsina State. He expressed appreciation to the people of Mai’adua for their overwhelming support and pledged to consolidate on the achievements of his administration if re-elected. “We have nothing to say but to thank God for the people of Mai’adua. We are grateful for the support we have received from women, youths and the elderly. This massive turnout shows that the people are satisfied with our achievements and leadership, especially in healthcare, education, teacher recruitment and empowerment.» “Please don’t make the mistake of electing 419 politicians. I know you are not in support of such politicians, and by the grace of God, we will reciprocate this confidence if re-elected. You have also demonstrated that you are genuine supporters and true admirers of the late President Muhammadu Buhari.” The governor also welcomed thousands of defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) into the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the development as further evidence of the ruling party’s growing popularity across the state. The rally’s highlight was the presentation of an Award of Excellence to Governor Radda by health workers in Mai’adua Local Government Area in recognition of what they described as his transformative leadership and commitment to strengthening the state’s healthcare sector. Earlier, Governor Radda commissioned the newly constructed Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) Dumurkul Division in Mai’adua Local Government Area. The security facility was built by the Chairman of Mai’adua Local Government, Hon. Mamman Salisu Na-Allahu, as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots security and enhance the fight against insecurity in the border communities. Commissioning the project, Governor Radda commended the council chairman for his foresight and commitment to safeguarding lives and property, stressing that security remains the cornerstone of his administration’s development agenda. He charged officers of the NSCDC to uphold professionalism, diligence, and discipline in the discharge of their duties while fostering stronger collaboration with other security agencies and host communities.
